title: Scheduler telemetry synthesis and proofing playbook
author: Miguel Santos
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the instrumentation contract, synthetic proofing pipeline, and troubleshooting runbook used to validate scheduler changes (policy, kernel hints, admission controller) before and during production rollout. It unifies metrics, traces, and synthetic benchmarks into a single reproducible proofing flow so we can confidently ship scheduler updates without regressions to SLOs.

Scope: scheduler policy changes, kernel hint propagation, admission signals, request shapers, and scheduler-side telemetry. This does NOT cover GPU driver upgrades or infra-level NIC/MTU changes — see infra runbooks for those.

Owner and stakeholders
- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling (on-call: kernel-scheduling team)
- Secondary owners: eng-sre (alert and incident ownership), eng-infra (capacity & hardware), eng-platform (observability ingestion)
- Review cadence: policy changes must be reviewed by two reviewers and validated with a full proofing run (see Proofing pipeline).

Contract: required telemetry signals and their semantics
Each scheduler change must produce or be compatible with the following signals. These are required for canary gating and alerting. Put this table in the change PR checklist and ensure synthetic jobs export the same metric names.

- scheduler.request_start_ts (histogram): time request entered scheduler queue
- scheduler.kernel_dispatch_latency_ms (histogram): kernel dispatch to first kernel-execution microsecond
- scheduler.kernel_queue_length{priority,cohort} (gauge): instantaneous queue depth per priority and cohort
- scheduler.kv_cache_hit_ratio{model_variant} (gauge): prefix/KV cache effective hit ratio seen by scheduler
- scheduler.kernels_inflight (gauge): number of kernels currently running on GPU(s) attributable to this scheduler shard
- scheduler.preemption_events_total{reason} (counter): count of preemption events and labeled reasons
- scheduler.admission_drop_total{reason,policy} (counter): dropped/short-circuited requests
- scheduler.latency_p50_ms, scheduler.latency_p95_ms, scheduler.latency_p99_ms (gauges): aggregate observed tail latency per window

Instrumentation checklist (pre-merge)
1) All metric names match the canonical contract above and are emitted for dev/prod canaries.
2) Metrics include the required labels: priority, cohort, model_variant, node_id, gpu_type.
3) Traces: every request must have a root span with scheduler:enqueue, scheduler:dispatch, kernel:launch, kernel:complete. Spans must propagate request_id and cohort tags.
4) Logs: scheduler-level events (admission decisions, preemptions, eviction reasons) must be structured JSON with timestamp, request_id, node_id, and decision_code.
5) Test harness: unit tests for policy logic + integration test that replays production-like traces with mocked kernel latencies.

Proofing pipeline (automated)
Purpose: run synthetic experiments that exercise the scheduler at representative load shapes and compare key metrics to a baseline. The pipeline runs locally in dev, then on a dedicated proofing cluster, and finally as a canary against a shadow production feed.

Steps (automated):
1. Build and instrumented image: build the scheduler change in an image tagged proofing/<change-id>.
2. Baseline snapshot: select the last known-good baseline snapshot (metrics and traces) from artifact storage.
3. Synthetic job generation: generate three workload shapes (steady, spike, long-tail) using the workload-builder. Each job produces: token length distribution, concurrency shape, and KV cache warmness profile.
4. Inject deterministic kernel latency perturbations: apply three perturbation profiles (nominal, 10% slow kernels, 1% slow outliers).
5. Run paired experiments: baseline vs candidate run for N=3 iterations each. Capture metrics, traces, and full request logs.
6. Compute differential report: compare p50/p95/p99 latency, admission_drop_total, preemption_events_total, and kv_cache_hit_ratio. Generate effect sizes and bootstrap confidence intervals.
7. Gate decision: if p99 regresses by >5% and admission_drop increases by >2x or preemption_events increase by >50%, fail gate. Otherwise, produce a human reviewable report.

Manual canary steps (if pipeline passes)
1. Deploy candidate to a 5% canary pool with traffic shadowing for 2 hours.
2. Activate synthetic short-burst test against canary nodes and verify matching telemetry.
3. Monitor the canary dashboard for 6 hours (metrics below). If any hard alert fires, trigger rollback.

Key proofing queries and example PromQL
- p95 latency for a cohort/variant: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(scheduler.latency_bucket[2m])) by (le, cohort, model_variant))
- admission drops rate: sum(rate(scheduler.admission_drop_total[1m])) by (policy)
- preemption spike detection (rule): increase(scheduler.preemption_events_total[5m]) > 0.5 * avg_over_time(increase(scheduler.preemption_events_total[1h])[1h:])

Alert thresholds and SLOs (gating & production)
- SLOs: latency_p95 <= 120ms for interactive small-chat cohort; p99 <= 400ms.
- Soft gate alerts (canary): p99 increase > 10% sustained for 10m OR admission_drop_total rate > 2x baseline for 15m. These trigger human review.
- Hard gate alerts (automatic rollback): p99 increase > 25% for 5m OR preemption_events_total increase > 100% for 5m OR kernel_queue_length per-GPU > 90% capacity for 3m.

Table: recommended sampling rates for proofing and production
- service_trace_sample_rate: proofing=1.0, canary=0.5, production=0.02
- scheduler_metric_resolution: proofing=5s, canary=10s, production=30s
- request_log_sampling: proofing=100%, canary=10%, production=0.1%

Diagnostic runbook: investigating scheduler-induced latency regression
1. Confirm regression window using p99 change detector (compare recent 10m to previous 1h).
2. Identify cohorts impacted: run per-cohort p99 query and list top-3 affected model_variant.
3. Check admission_drop_total and preemption_events_total for correlated spikes.
4. Attach traces: pull 20 traces sampled during the regression window for the affected cohort. Look for: long scheduler:enqueue spans, repeated preemption, or kernel:launch retries.
5. Inspect kernel metrics: kernel_dispatch_latency_ms and kernels_inflight. If kernel_dispatch_latency_ms increased while kernels_inflight unchanged, suspect kernel queuing within GPU driver or interconnect. If kernels_inflight jumped, suspect scheduling admission miscalibration.
6. Cross-check KV cache metrics: a sudden drop in kv_cache_hit_ratio often amplifies p99 due to longer decode generation chains.
7. If root cause points to policy change, disable the policy flag (feature-flag rollback) and observe metric reversion for 10 minutes. If rollback undoes regression, open an incident with severity P1 and follow incident process.

Quick commands and snippets
- Pull traces for a request_id (example):
  curl -s "https://traces.internal/api/trace?request_id=abcd-1234" | jq '.'
- Export scheduler metrics snapshot (example):
  promtool snapshot query 'sum(rate(scheduler.latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, cohort, model_variant)' --output json > /tmp/scheduler_snapshot.json
- Run synthetic local job (workload-builder):
  wb run --shape spike --concurrency 120 --model small-chat --kv-warmness 0.7 --out artifacts/run-<id>

Visibility and dashboards
- Canary dashboard must include: p50/p95/p99 by cohort, admission_drop rate, preemption_events, kv_cache_hit_ratio, kernel_queue_length heatmap by node.
- Proofing report components: paired-differential graphs (latency, drops, preemptions), trace waterfall samples, and an artifacts section with raw logs and run configuration.

Rollout gating matrix (summary)
1. Unit tests + instrumentation checks: required before merge.
2. Automated proofing pipeline: must pass.
3. Canary deployment (5%): must pass soft gates for 6 hours.
4. Gradual rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring windows at each step (30m, 1h, 2h).

Rollback procedure (fast rollback)
1. Set feature flag to baseline (feature-flag disable <change-id>).
2. Restart scheduler processes on canary nodes with baseline image: kubectl rollout restart daemonset/scheduler -n serving-canary
3. Validate metric reversion: p99 returns to within 3% of baseline in 10 minutes.
4. If not recovered, escalate to eng-sre and open emergency bridge.

Appendix: proofing artifact naming conventions
- proofing/<change-id>/run-<iteration>/<workload-shape>/<snapshot-timestamp>
- Each artifact dir must include: metrics.json, traces.jsonl, run-config.yaml, raw-logs.jsonl, compare-report.html

FAQ and notes
- Why synthetic proofing? Production traffic can be noisy; synthetic proofing isolates scheduler logic against repeatable inputs and controlled kernel perturbations.
- How to add new telemetry? Add metric to contract and update instrumentation checklist. New metrics require at least one synthetic job that validates cardinality and label density.
- Expected time for a full proofing run: 45–90 minutes depending on artifact upload times.
